title: queuey.deploy.json
description: A declarative deployment file — queuey.deploy.json by default. Describes the workspace's delivery defaults and each queue's behaviour and destination, so a deploy converges Queuey from something reviewable in a pull request.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema this file follows, for editors and agents: the published one, or a local copy written by queuey schema. Ignored when the file is applied.

tenant.description: The workspace (ten_…) this file describes. Optional — the CLI falls back to the tenant in the connection config, so the same file can be applied to staging and production.

workspace.description: The workspace — the layer every queue inherits from when it says nothing itself.

environment.description: The workspace's environment: dev, test, staging or prod, lowest first. Queuey treats a workspace without one as prod. An API key may raise it towards prod, but only a person lowers it, in the Queuey console, so apply is refused when the file names a lower environment than the workspace has. A file applied to several workspaces takes it from a variable, such as ${QUEUEY_WORKSPACE_ENVIRONMENT}.

ordering.description: Lane strategy for every queue that does not override it: fifo, bykey, besteffort.

dlqEnabled.description: Whether a dead-letter queue collects events the receiver rejected.

retentionDays.description: How many days events are retained.

idempotent.description: Whether the receiver handles the same event twice safely. Then Queuey sends an event again after a timeout or a conflict (409, 412, 423 or 428). Otherwise a timeout holds the queue until a person resumes it, and a conflict stops the event. It does not deduplicate publishes.

backoff.description: How long to wait between attempts, for every queue that does not say. The number of attempts is not a setting.

baseDelayMs.description: The first wait, in milliseconds: above 0, and at most 3600000 (one hour) unless a longer wait is already in place. Each later wait doubles, up to MaxDelayMs.

maxDelayMs.description: The longest wait between two attempts, in milliseconds: above 0, not below the first wait, and at most 86400000 (24 hours) unless a longer wait is already in place.

jitter.description: full spreads the waits randomly so retries do not arrive in step; none does not.

delivery.description: Where events are delivered — the base every queue appends its path to.

baseUrl.description: Base URL every inheriting queue delivers to.

authMode.description: Outbound auth mode: None, Bearer, ApiKey, Basic or OAuth2ClientCredentials.

credentialRef.description: The name of a stored credential to authenticate with. Never the secret itself.

authHeaderName.description: Header name for ApiKey auth (e.g. X-Api-Key).

method.description: HTTP method: POST, PUT or PATCH.

signing.description: Outbound request signing. Null leaves signing untouched.

credentialRef.description: The name of the stored signing secret (or its cred_… id). Never the secret itself.

rateLimit.description: Send budget. Null leaves the budget untouched.

ingress.description: How arriving events are read: ingress auth, and where the type and key come from.

authMode.description: What the ingress edge demands of a publisher: None, ApiKey, SignedRequest or ApiKeyAndSignedRequest.

eventType.description: Where the event type is read from. Null leaves it as it is.

from.description: Where the value is read: header, query, or body, the top level of the JSON you post. Required whenever name is not empty.

name.description: The header, query parameter, or body field to read. Required: "" removes the source, so the value is no longer read from anywhere.

groupKey.description: Where the group key is read from — and, by declaring it, what to lane on.

from.description: Where the value is read: header, query, or body, the top level of the JSON you post. Required whenever name is not empty.

name.description: The header, query parameter, or body field to read. Required: "" removes the source, so the value is no longer read from anywhere.

successStatusCode.description: The status the ingress returns on accept. Default 202. Some senders are stricter than the HTTP spec and treat anything but 200 as a failed webhook, so those queues set 200.

signedRequest.description: The provider signature the ingress verifies: a template, such as stripe, and the credential holding the provider's signing secret. Checked while AuthMode is SignedRequest or ApiKeyAndSignedRequest.

template.description: The signed-request template from Queuey's catalogue: stripe, or queuey for Queuey's own scheme, which verifies with the sending API client's signing key and takes no credential.

credentialRef.description: The name of the credential holding the provider's signing secret (or its cred_… id): letters, digits and . _ : @ / -, starting with a letter or digit, since Queuey shows a name it waits for in suggested commands. Store it with queuey credentials set --name <name> --type HmacSigning --key-id <name> --from-env <VARIABLE>. A stored credential whose name has other characters is named by its id.

queues.description: The queues to converge, keyed by queue name.

additionalProperties.description: One queue's declaration: behaviour, and optionally its own destination.

mode.description: deliver or logOnly. Omit it and a queue this file creates delivers when it has a destination (its own delivery.url or the workspace's base URL) and logs events until it has one; an existing queue keeps its mode. Pausing is not a mode and never set by a deploy.

backoff.description: How long to wait between attempts. The number of attempts is not a setting: Queuey decides what each failure needs.

baseDelayMs.description: The first wait, in milliseconds: above 0, and at most 3600000 (one hour) unless a longer wait is already in place. Each later wait doubles, up to MaxDelayMs.

maxDelayMs.description: The longest wait between two attempts, in milliseconds: above 0, not below the first wait, and at most 86400000 (24 hours) unless a longer wait is already in place.

jitter.description: full spreads the waits randomly so retries do not arrive in step; none does not.

filter.description: Which events this queue delivers. Omit it to leave the queue's filter as it is; declare it with "conditions": [] to remove the filter, so the queue delivers every event.

conditions.description: The conditions, required whenever a filter is declared. An empty list delivers every event, which is how a filter is removed, so a filter without the list is refused rather than read as empty.

items.description: One condition on a top-level JSON body field.

field.description: The top-level field of the JSON body, exactly as it is written there: no whitespace around it.

op.description: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains or exists.

value.description: The value to compare with. gt, gte, lt and lte take a plain number written like 1.5. exists takes no value.

ordering.description: Delivery ordering: fifo, bykey or besteffort.

dlqEnabled.description: Whether a dead-letter queue collects events the receiver rejected.

idempotent.description: Whether the receiver handles the same event twice safely. Then Queuey sends an event again after a timeout or a conflict (409, 412, 423 or 428). Otherwise a timeout holds the queue until a person resumes it, and a conflict stops the event. It does not deduplicate publishes.

delivery.description: This queue's destination. Omit it — the usual case — and the queue inherits the workspace. A relative url appends to the workspace base, which is the shape to reach for.

kind.description: Where the queue's events go: http, to its URL, or localForward, to a connected queuey listen session, for a queue in a development workspace. Omit it to leave the kind as it is. A local listener's address belongs to its session (--forward-to), never to this file, and the queue keeps its URL for when it delivers over HTTP again. A file applied to several workspaces takes it from a variable, such as ${QUEUEY_ORDERS_DELIVERY_KIND}.

url.description: Where this queue delivers. A relative path (/orders) appends to the workspace base — the shape to reach for, since moving hosts is then one workspace edit. An absolute URL overrides the workspace outright.

inherit.description: Hands the destination back to the workspace, discarding this queue's own override.

authMode.description: Outbound auth mode for this queue only. Null inherits the workspace.

credentialRef.description: The name of a stored credential. Never the secret itself.

signing.description: Outbound request signing for this queue only.

credentialRef.description: The name of the stored signing secret (or its cred_… id). Never the secret itself.

rateLimit.description: Send budget for this queue only.

ingress.description: How this queue reads arriving events, when it differs from the workspace. Omit it and the queue inherits — which is what you want unless one producer sends a different shape.

authMode.description: What the ingress edge demands of a publisher: None, ApiKey, SignedRequest or ApiKeyAndSignedRequest.

eventType.description: Where the event type is read from. Null leaves it as it is.

groupKey.description: Where the group key is read from — and, by declaring it, what to lane on.

successStatusCode.description: The status the ingress returns on accept. Default 202. Some senders are stricter than the HTTP spec and treat anything but 200 as a failed webhook, so those queues set 200.

signedRequest.description: The provider signature the ingress verifies: a template, such as stripe, and the credential holding the provider's signing secret. Checked while AuthMode is SignedRequest or ApiKeyAndSignedRequest.

profiles.description: The values this file takes per environment, by profile name (dev, prod …): what its ${VAR} references expand to with --profile <name>, so promoting a change is a pull request against the file. The connection (the key, the license, the hosts) is never here: it lives with the user, in the profile of the same name in ~/.queuey/config.json.

additionalProperties.description: The values a deployment file takes in one environment: what its ${VAR} references expand to with --profile <name>. Never a secret: the file is committed, and the key that applies it lives with the user.

variables.description: The value of each ${VAR} in this environment, by variable name, such as QUEUEY_TENANT: a workspace id, a base URL, a delivery kind. A value is taken as it is written, never expanded again, and one that looks like a secret is refused. A variable the profile leaves out comes from the environment, as without a profile; one set in both, to different values, is an error.
